Explanation: Option (a): This option partially captures a factual element of the passage—the
ethnic violence in Manipur—but mistakenly narrows the scope of the author’s discussion. While
the text does highlight that the rise in crimes against Scheduled Tribes (STs) is largely due to the
Manipur violence, the passage also situates this within broader national patterns: high crime
rates in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, growing tribal vulnerability, and the government’s
delayed data publication. The main idea is not that Manipur distorts crime statistics but that the
surge in certain categories (crimes against STs, cybercrime) coexists with improvement in others
(decline in murders) By treating Manipur as the central or sole cause of India’s crime trends,
option (a) overstates a local phenomenon and misses the author’s more comprehensive critique of
governance and uneven social protection. Thus, option (a) is too narrow and fails to reflect the full
complexity of the argument.
Option (b): This option focuses exclusively on the delay in the NCRB report, but the passage treats
that point as context, not the central message. The author opens with a reference to the report’s
“delay by a year,” connecting it to “a worrying trend of postponed surveys, reports, and even the
Census.” However, this serves as a framing observation about institutional inefficiency, not the
main concern. The core of the passage shifts immediately to substantive crime data—the 2.8%
drop in murders, the 28.8% rise in crimes against STs, and the 31.2% surge in cybercrime. The
commentary emphasizes contrasting trends and governance lapses in handling ethnic and
technological crimes, not merely bureaucratic delays. Therefore, option (b) mistakes the backdrop
(delay) for the central insight (divergent crime patterns and policy failure).. Hence, option (b) is
incomplete and secondary relative to the main argument.

Option (c): This choice is factually inaccurate because the passage explicitly contrasts change in
India’s crime trends, not continuity. It notes that while murder cases have fallen by 2.8%, crimes
against STs have skyrocketed by nearly 29%, and cyber offences by over 31%. These sharp
statistical variations refute any claim of “unchanged patterns” or “stable rates.” Moreover, the
author highlights specific shifts in geography and cause—Manipur’s ethnic violence, high ST
vulnerability in central India, and the digital surge in cybercrime. By asserting that crime
patterns “remain unchanged,” (C) erases the very dynamics that the passage seeks to analyze. The
author’s argument is that India’s crime landscape is evolving unevenly: traditional violent crimes
are declining while socially and technologically mediated crimes are rising. Hence, option (c)
misrepresents the text’s analytical contrast and therefore is incorrect.
Option (d): This option perfectly encapsulates the main idea of the passage by acknowledging its
two-fold focus: contrasting statistical trends and governance implications. The author presents a
paradoxical picture—a modest 2.8% decline in murders suggesting improved control of
interpersonal violence, juxtaposed with a 28.8% surge in crimes against STs (linked to Manipur
and tribal vulnerability) and a 31.2% rise in cybercrimes. Together, these figures expose both the
shifting nature of crime and institutional weaknesses in addressing emerging challenges. The
mention of the government’s delayed reporting reinforces a pattern of administrative complacency,
while the commentary on preventable violence (“which a more effective government could have
mitigated”) explicitly connects data to governance failure. Therefore, option (d) captures both the
statistical contrast and the moral critique central to the author’s argument: India’s crime profile
reveals uneven progress and policy neglect. It’s a balanced synthesis of fact, context, and
evaluation—hence, the correct answer.

Explanation: Passage Explanation: The passage emphasizes that every individual possesses a
divine spark capable of greatness. True excellence arises not merely from talent but from
connecting one’s abilities to a higher purpose—serving others or the divine, as exemplified by
Olympic champion Eric Liddell. Success becomes meaningful when rooted in gratitude rather than
greed. The text also links loneliness to self-centeredness, urging compassion and _ heartfelt
connection with others as the way to overcome isolation and experience true fulfillment.
Option (a): This is the core assumption behind the entire passage. The author begins by asserting
that “we are all wired for greatness” and that “everyone carries the same divine spark.” These
statements assume that divinity or faith functions as an activating force that transforms ordinary
talent into extraordinary performance. The example of Eric Liddell, who believed “God made me to
run, and I will run for God,” is central evidence: his faith, not external coaching or material aid,
propelled him to Olympic victory. Similarly, the author insists that “what you do matters more
than how talented you are,” and that excellence flows when one dedicates their work to a higher
cause—community, country, or God. The repeated emphasis on “connecting with the Spirit” and
offering one’s gift “back in gratitude” reveals the assumption that faith channels effort into
excellence. Without divine alignment, talent remains directionless; with it, greatness manifests
meaningfully.
Option (b): This option misinterprets the author’s message by reducing spirituality to worldly
achievement. The passage never equates spiritual awareness with fame, wealth, or recognition.
On the contrary, it critiques such materialistic motivations: “If you use your gift only to make

money, you'll remain ordinary.” The author’s idea of success is moral and transcendent, not social
or economic. Even when using Eric Liddell’s Olympic win as an example, the emphasis is on his
faithful intention rather than his medal. The author views spiritual awareness as a path to inner
excellence and gratitude, not as a strategy for outward acclaim. Furthermore, the latter half of the
passage shifts toward emotional and spiritual connection, warning that self-centeredness and
obsession with image lead to “loneliness’—a sign that true fulfillment lies in humility and
compassion, not popularity. Hence, option (b) distorts the argument by confusing inner spiritual
growth with external validation.
Option (c): This option directly contradicts the author’s values. The passage explicitly warns
against self-absorption and purely personal ambition. The author writes, “When you're
preoccupied with yourself — your looks, comfort, image — you feel isolated even in a crowd.” This
reflects a moral critique of egocentric ambition. Instead, excellence, in the author’s view, flows
from dedication to a higher or collective purpose: “Dedicate your talent to a higher purpose — your
company, your community, your country.” Such phrasing suggests that one’s individual effort finds
meaning only through service to others or gratitude to the divine. Thus, the author’s framework is
altruistic and spiritual, not individualistic or competitive. Claiming that excellence emerges from
personal ambition alone ignores the passage’s repeated insistence on humility, connection, and
service as spiritual disciplines. Therefore, option (c) completely misrepresents the philosophical
basis of the argument.
Option (d): This option is diametrically opposed to the author’s argument. The text portrays faith
as a transformative driver of performance and excellence, not a source of passive comfort. Eric
Liddell’s example proves this: faith doesn’t soothe him into complacency—it energises him to run
“for God,” leading to Olympic triumph. The author declares, “Connect with the Spirit and you'll
rise above every obstacle to achieve excellence.” Here, divine belief fuels motivation and
perseverance. Similarly, the statement “When you realise your ability isn’t yours—it’s a divine
blessing” links humility before God with the experience of perfection or “magic.” Faith, therefore,
is depicted as an active force—it ignites effort, deepens purpose, and converts potential into
extraordinary achievement. Far from providing emotional comfort alone, divine belief gives moral
direction and inner strength. Thus, option (d) is inconsistent with the text’s message that faith
transforms effort into transcendence.

“Dedicate your talent to a higher purpose — your company, your community, your country.” This
already recognises worldly contexts such as work or national service. Therefore, even if ambition
coexists with belief, the divine element can still provide direction and moral grounding. Rather

purpose, where faith gives ambition meaning. Thus, option (d) does not weaken the argument.

Explanation: Passage Explanation: The passage describes how unusually destructive monsoon
events across multiple Indian states — flash floods, landslides, and crop losses — occurred even
with rainfall only 8% above normal, showing that factors beyond local weather are at play.
Scientists link these extreme events to rapid Arctic warming, which is happening nearly four
times faster than the global average. Melting Arctic ice disturbs jet streams, the high-altitude air
currents that normally stabilize monsoon systems. As these streams weaken and meander,
monsoons increasingly stall, intensify, or shift unpredictably, triggering widespread flooding and
devastation across India.
Option (a): This statement is clearly contradicted by the passage. While local factors such as
“fragile geology” and “unchecked construction” are acknowledged, the author explicitly argues that
these are only partial causes of India’s flooding disasters. The key idea is that “scientific analysis
points towards a much wider and more complex chain of causation—stretching all the way to the
Arctic Circle.” The text highlights Arctic warming as a global climatic force whose effects cascade
into the South Asian monsoon system by altering jet streams. Therefore, saying that the floods are

“entirely the result of local deforestation and urban expansion without any global influence”
oversimplifies and directly opposes the author’s argument. The passage is precisely written to
expand our understanding beyond local explanations and link Indian monsoon irregularities to
planetary-scale climate dynamics, not to exclude them. Hence, option (a) is false because it denies
the global interconnection that the passage establishes.
Option (b): This is the correct answer and accurately captures the author’s scientific reasoning.
The passage explains that the Arctic is warming “nearly four times faster than the global
average,” and this unprecedented rate of warming “disrupts jet streams—those fast-moving air
currents that shape weather patterns.” Normally, these jet streams guide and stabilise the South
Asian monsoon. However, as the Arctic’s sea ice diminishes, the weakened and meandering
streams cause weather systems to “stall, intensify, or shift unpredictably.” This results in the kind
of erratic monsoon activity described earlier: flash floods, cloudbursts, and landslides across India,
even with only 8% above-normal rainfall. Therefore, it logically follows that Arctic warming and
jet stream disruption contribute to intensified and unpredictable monsoon behaviour in South
Asia. The author uses this causal link to shift attention from local environmental mismanagement
to global climate interdependence, making (B) the most faithful inference from the passage.
Option (c): This option directly contradicts the author’s main thesis. The passage explicitly rejects
the idea that Arctic warming is a “polar-only” issue. It states that “this rapid ice melt is not just an
isolated polar phenomenon but one with cascading effects on atmospheric systems around the
globe.” The word “cascading” signals that changes in the Arctic have ripple effects far beyond their
geographic origin—altering weather patterns, jet stream paths, and consequently monsoon
systems in South Asia. Thus, the author’s entire point is that the Arctic is climatically entangled
with lower latitudes, and its warming has a destabilising effect on tropical weather cycles. By
claiming the opposite—that Arctic warming “affects only polar regions’—(C) ignores both the
stated evidence and the causal framework outlined by the text. It would completely misrepresent
the argument’s intent, which is to globalise our understanding of India’s climate crises. Hence,
option (c) is incorrect.
Option (d): This option is factually inconsistent with the passage’s description of India’s worsening
monsoon disasters. The text vividly recounts widespread floods, landslides, and destruction across
“Kishtwar, Uttarkashi, Pithoragarh, Manali, Kangra, Marathwada, Karnataka, and Punjab’—all
caused by unusually intense monsoon events. It emphasises that such devastation occurred
despite rainfall being only “8% above-normal.” This suggests that monsoon-related disasters have
become more frequent and severe, not less. The passage also uses words like “alarming,” » &, “washed
away bridges,” and “buried village hutments” to depict escalating climate volatility. Therefore,
claiming that disasters have “declined” directly contradicts the substance of the narrative. The
passage portrays the situation as a climate emergency, not an improvement. Thus, option (d) is
false, as it misreads both the factual data and the implied trend of increasing disaster frequency
and intensity.

Therefore, this statement is consistent with the passage’s balanced view that both human-made

Option (c): The author would also agree with this statement because it accurately reflects the

Option (d): This statement also aligns with the author’s reasoning and reinforces a central

He notes that these currents typically “guide and stabilise the flow of monsoon systems into South
Asia.” However, because of Arctic warming, they now tend to weaken, meander, or stall, leading to
erratic rainfall distribution and intensified floods. Thus, the behaviour of jet streams—whether
stable or disturbed—plays a crucial role in determining monsoon patterns. The author’s explicit
phrasing confirms this view. Therefore, option (d) is consistent with the text’s scientific
explanation, meaning he would agree, not disagree, with it.
